repo.description:
### Summary

Write operations submitted through the internal batch endpoint were authorized against the source named on the outer envelope rather than the source actually targeted, letting a base Editor write to a source configured as data-read-only.

### Details

`internal.controller.ts` builds each batch sub-request with `Object.create(req)` and replaces only `query` and `body`, so authorization-relevant properties already resolved by the ID-extraction middleware - notably the source id derived from the envelope's table - were inherited by the sub-request. The dispatcher also accepted every registered operation except a nested batch, including the data-write operations, even though the SDK describes the batch set as read-only. A caller could therefore name a table from a writable source on the envelope and a table belonging to a data-read-only source inside a `dataUpdate`, `dataInsert` or `dataDelete` sub-operation: the read-only assertion in `extract-ids.middleware.ts` evaluated the writable decoy source and allowed the request, while `data-table.service.ts` resolved the inner table and performed the write without re-checking the restriction on the actual target source.

### Impact

Requires an authenticated base Editor role, or any other base role carrying data-write permission, plus knowledge of workspace, base and table identifiers that are ordinarily visible to a base member. Such a user could insert, update, move or delete records in a source the base owner had explicitly configured as data-read-only, corrupting or destroying data in an attached production database and defeating the source-level write boundary.

### Credit

This issue was reported by [@l0h1nth](https://github.com/l0h1nth).
repo.summary: Read-Only Source Restriction Bypass via Internal Batch API
